DILG BAGONG PIUP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph s. 2011 Ott-G OPINION NO. JUL 04 ATTY. CHAD JOREL V. HERNANDEZ First Oceanic Property Management, Inc. 5/F Tower B, One Campus Place 1080 Campus Avenue, McKinley Town Center Pinagsama, Taguig City Dear Atty. Hernandez: This has reference to your letter dated November 20, 2023, requesting this Department's on whether a property management firm can be required to pay local business tax in the city where it deploys its employees to administer the building belonging to its principal but does not maintain a branch or sales outlet therein. Hereunder are the pertinent factual antecedents as culled in your letter: Your client, First Oceanic Property Management, Inc. ("FOPM"), is a property management firm primarily responsible for administering the common areas and facilities of the residential and commercial buildings exclusively developed by its principal, Megaworld Corporation ("Megaworld"), which are located across the Philippines, including Iloilo City. The FOPM, pursuant to its Articles of Incorporation, acts as a service provider of condominiums, office buildings, villages, facilities, townhouses, projects, parking areas, and requiring the management and administration of common areas, including the amenities, equipment, elevators, and machinery for the common benefits of owners, occupants, and tenants; the delivery of direct and/or supervisory property management services, which primarily cover customer service, housekeeping, engineering, finance, administration, and security. With regard to some of the buildings of Megaworld located in Iloilo City, FOPM was chosen by the former to administer such buildings. To formalize such engagement, an agreement between FOPM and Megaworld's affiliates, namely Megaworld Real Estate Investment Trust Property Managers, Inc. ("MPMI") and Megaworld Real Estate Investment Trust Fund Managers, Inc. ("MFMI"), was subsequently entered into in Taguig City, where its head offices are also located. It is in Taguig City that FOPM pays its local business taxes based on 100% of its gross sales, and for which a business permit is issued. The payment for the services of FOPM, including those rendered in Iloilo City, is also being remitted to Taguig City. Also, the corresponding receipts and sales invoices Of FOPM are solely issued from its head office in Taguig City, and it has no other registered offices in other parts of the country. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

FOPM does not have a branch or office in Iloilo City. The buildings that FOPM handles in Iloilo City belong to its principals. In addition, FOPM's offices therein are only being lent by its principals without any charge and for temporary use, considering that the same is needed in pursuance of its contractual obligations, particularly the collection of Common Use of Service Area (CUSA) fees and association dues that are considered the income of the principals. Such fees and dues are considered the income of the principals of FOPM who are duly registered in Iloilo City. FOPM's contracts are only for a specific term of one (I) year and are even subject to its principal's pre-termination, including those services provided in the properties in Iloilo City. Therefore, FOPM's services in Iloilo City are being rendered on a temporary basis and can be discounted by MPMI and MFMI at any given time, with or without cause. The City Treasurer of Iloilo claims that FOPM must pay local business taxes in Iloilo City. On September 25, 2023, a summons was issued to FOPM, requiring FOPM to explain why it failed to pay local business tax and secure a mayor's permit from the city government of Iloilo City. In response, the FOPM sent a letter to the City Treasurer to explain its position that it does not maintain a branch or sales outlet in Iloilo City nor receive any income therein. The City Treasurer asserted that FOPM is doing business in Iloilo City and stated that "the contractual obligation that binds between the FOPM and Megaworld to render services as property management in Iloilo City with a fee or association dues attests that the FOPM is doing business in Iloilo City regardless if it is being lent free of charge." Hence, the subject query. Prefatorily, we take particular note that FOPM does not currently maintain a branch or sales outlet in Iloilo City. As represented, FOPM's principal location and head offices are in Taguig City, where it is subject to local business taxes based on its gross sales. It is also noted that FOPM's contractual engagement with Megaworld's affiliates for the administration of buildings in Iloilo City was formalized by virtue of an agreement entered into in Taguig City. Furthermore, it is well to note that FOPM operations in Iloilo City involve the temporary use of office space provided by its principals for the purpose of fulfilling contractual obligations, particularly in the collection of CUSA fees and association dues. Such dues and fees, as represented, constitute income for FOPM's principals, who are duly registered entities in Iloilo City. Having laid down the foregoing, we take cognizance that the issue at hand appears to be relatively analogous to an issue we have previously addressed in DILG Legal Opinion No. 69, Series of 2018. The legal question at hand bears significant resemblance to the issue proffered in the said Opinion. Precisely, the question proffered is: Whether an independent contractor may be required to pay business taxes in municipalities or cities where it deploys employees but where it does not maintain branch or sales outlets. Our view thereon is in the negative, citing the Court of Tax Appeals pronouncement in an En Banc Decision in the case of City of Makati v. the Municipality of Bakun and Luzon Hydro Corporation. Anchored on the aforesaid Court decision and Section 150 Of the Local Govemment Code of 19911, we opined in this wise: "Section 150. Situs of the Tax. — Page 2 of3

"[In] order for the municipality/city to collect business taxes from an establishment, the same should be a branch or sales office where actual sales/transactions were conducted and not merely an administrative office. The branch or sales office shall likewise record the sale or transaction in the principal office." Section 150(a) of the Code is categorical when it provides that "in cases where there is no such branch or sales outlet in the city or municipality where the sale or transaction is made, the sale shall be duly recorded in the principal office and the taxes due shall accrue and shall be paid to such city or municipality." We are of the view that FOPM activities in Iloilo City are ancillary to its primary operations based in Taguig. Further, it is worth noting that the income derived from FOPM's activities in Iloilo City does not accrue to it; rather, it accrues to its principals, who are the recipients of such income and are obligated to pay local taxes in Iloilo City as duly registered entities. Notwithstanding the foregoing, we shall still defer to the position of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) of the Department of Finance (DOF) on the issue of imposition of business taxes on FOPM. Notwithstanding, this Department opines that FOPM is still required to secure a business/mayor's permit in Iloilo City for regulatory purposes. It is well within the authority of the mayor to require business establishments and firms operating under his jurisdiction to secure a mayor's permit, as has been consistently held by the Supreme Court in the plethora of cases it has decided. Such authority stems from the local government's police power, which is deemed crucial for ensuring that businesses and establishments adhere to local ordinances, thereby safeguarding the interests and welfare of the general public and maintaining public order. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, e thority of the Secretary: ATTY R. LLAMAS retary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA'JVRULLLS-LRALLD/jam cc: Dir. MARIA LOURDES L. AGUSTIN, CESO Ill Regional Director, NCR 4/F Annex Building — SRA Sugar Center Compound, North Avenue Diliman, Quezon City (a) For purposes of collection of the taxes under Section 143 of this Code, manufacturers, assemblers, repackers, brewers, distillers, rectifiers and compounders of liquor, distilled spirits and wines, millers, producers, exporters, wholesalers, distributors, dealers, contractors, banks and other financial institutions, and other businesses, maintaining or operating branch or sales outlet elsewhere shall record the sale in the branch or sales outlet making the sale or transaction, and the tax thereon shall accrue and shall be paid to the municipality where such branch or sales outlet is located. In cases where there is no such branch or sales outlet in the city or municipality where the sale or transaction is made, the sale shall be duly recorded in the principal office and the taxes due shall accrue and shall be paid to such city or municipality.
